chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed his wealth in the way of Allah.
He said: Give it to the one he bequeathed it for, even if he was a Jew or a Christian.
Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'So whoever alters it after he has heard it, then its sin is only upon those who alter it.'
ai.seo_question: Does the religion of the beneficiary affect the validity of a bequest in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that a bequest is binding according to the testator's specific designation, even if the recipient is a non-Muslim, highlighting the principle of honoring the deceased's intent. This ruling is grounded in Surah Al-Baqarah 2:181, which warns against altering the will after hearing it, thereby preserving the original command. The narration underscores the flexibility of Islamic inheritance law in accommodating diverse religious affiliations for charitable bequests.
